newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steady but supply seen drowning prices.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steady but supply seen drowning prices.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices were steady on Wednesday but end-users and brokers said demand was flagging and an anticipated rising supply of cargoes was pushing physical assessments lower.
An late selloff in Brent crude also knocked swaps prices off their session highs. Jan ended unchanged at $222 after offers reached $225, they said.
"There is a lot of naphtha...It is definitely long," said one trader. "You will see a lot of cargoes coming onto the market."
"The physical quote is really distressed," he argued.
A 25,000-30,000 Algerian cargo of pipeline spec material will soon be back onto the market after going through the chain, he said.
Two more cargoes of Egyptian and Algeria material, of similar size, will also be available at the end of the month, he said.
Liquidity for Dec swaps dried up but prices were generally seen anywhere from flat to $2-$3 under Jan.
Traders said the physical market remained in contango, reinforced by talk of a 6,000 tonne Russian cargo believed to have been sold at a discount of mean minus $3 on Tuesday.
But the trader said it was offered at mean minus $3 and bid at mean minus $10, so it was unclear if the material was sold. The cargo may go into storage and hit the market in January, he said.
"There is not much buying from end-users," a broker said. "If you want to sell small parcels, it is hard to find homes."
"If you talk to the end-users, (cargo prices) are at $215. If you talk to a trader, it's at $225," he said.
Cargo prices were very notionally set at $219/$223 cif, but sources agreed any deals would likely get down below this level.
